digests.title: TLDR Tech — 2026-07-30
digests.tagline: Starlink cell network 🛰️, DoorDash drones 🚁, inside ChatGPT optimizations 👨‍💻

stories.headline: SpaceX looks to compete with the carriers (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: SpaceX has been hunting for a spectrum that works well in cities and dense areas for its wireless network. It is considering buying competitors to acquire the spectrum or competing at a government auction set for next year. The company has expressed interest in building its own terrestrial networks and has demonstrated a prototype mobile handset to some investors. Entering into the mobile market is capital intensive, so SpaceX could ultimately choose not to follow through on these plans.

stories.headline: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar tells employees that annualized revenue in July topped all of Q2 (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: OpenAI's annualized recurring revenue in July exceeded the company's entire second quarter. The growth was driven by the release of the company's GPT-5.6 series of models and ChatGPT Work, as well as growing adoption of Codex. OpenAI is under pressure to justify its $852 billion valuation as it prepares for its IPO. It has been racing to bring in new users to generate the revenue needed to help support its infrastructure spending plans.

stories.headline: DoorDash Gets FAA Nod to Run Its Own Drone Delivery Program (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: DoorDash has received permission from the FAA to deliver packages by drone at altitudes below 400 feet. The drones will be built in the company's in-house robotics unit, DoorDash Labs. DoorDash Air aims to cater to any merchant, anywhere. The company will release more information later this year on its drones and how its drone program will fit into DoorDash's broader ecosystem.

stories.headline: China Closes the Satellite Gap in Space Race With the US (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: China has accelerated its deployment of civilian and military hardware into orbit. The country's growing constellations of satellites could help it track events on Earth in real time and in greater detail than ever before. This has raised concerns among US officials, who see China's growing array of space-based capabilities as a quest to displace the US as the pre-eminent space power. Western analysts say that China is leading the world in research in sensors and satellite positioning technologies.

stories.headline: Treat prompt changes like code deploys (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: Prompts are dependencies. Changing them can shift downstream behavior with no warning, no failing build, and no obvious signal in the request pipeline. Treat prompts exactly like any other artifact that can change production behavior. Test them, give them a gate, and default that gate to blocking until proven otherwise.

stories.headline: How ChatGPT Optimizes its Agent Loop: Harness, API, and Inference (26 minute read)
stories.blurb: AI labs are moving faster than ever. However, capability is only half of the picture. Optimizing the cost per successful task makes models more affordable and less costly to serve. This article discusses techniques adopted in frontier labs to make API applications more efficient. It covers what happens when requests are sent to an AI agent, how the harness layer cuts repeated work, and more.

stories.headline: The Rise of Million-Dollar Companies With Just One Employee (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: A new class of entrepreneurs is launching and running new million-dollar companies on their own. AI's ability to handle various administrative tasks makes it useful for launching solo businesses in many fields. The effect of one-person businesses on the labor market remains to be seen. While many people are worried AI will limit employment opportunities, these solo operators show how the technology can also open new doors.

stories.headline: Why compute might get 10x+ more expensive in coming years (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: Labs do not want to spend greater and greater shares of compute on inference. The point of inference revenue is to convince investors to spend more money to buy more compute to train bigger models. Spending too much on compute on inference signals that progress has stalled because it's not worth investing more in training. Labs believe that their models will continue to get better, so this only means that compute will get more expensive.

stories.headline: AI Companies Are Recruiting Electricians and Carpenters by the Thousands (12 minute read)
stories.blurb: The data center boom is pulling skilled trade workers into remote locations with some of the highest pay and bonuses the industry has ever seen.

stories.headline: numbat (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: numbat provides endpoint visibility into AI agent activity with local detection, optional pre-action blocking, and forensic reconstruction.

stories.headline: The Cold Email (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: It may be awkward and weird and strange, but it's usually worth the shot to send a cold email.

stories.headline: AI's 2008 Moment (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: Open-weight models are already being built into critical systems in the US.

stories.headline: How China's Venture Ecosystem Works (12 minute read)
stories.blurb: Chinese founders face more pressure and liability, which results in more competent and ruthless companies, but also creates incentives for more froth and fraud.

stories.headline: Highlights From The Discourse On The Hugging Face Incident (35 minute read)
stories.blurb: There is a consistent pattern of OpenAI's alignment strategies working less well than Anthropic's.

digests.title: TLDR AI — 2026-07-30
digests.tagline: OpenAI tops ARC-AGI-3 📈, GPT-5.6 efficiency ⚙️, AlphaFold team dissolution 🧬

stories.headline: Thinking Machines Cofounder Joined OpenAI (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Thinking Machines co-founder Lilian Weng left the startup after citing health effects from sustained stress and workload, then joined OpenAI. She said the pace required by the startup had become physically unsustainable.

stories.headline: SpaceXAI launches Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0 on Agent Builder (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0 is now available at $0.09 per audio minute. grok-voice-latest will switch over to the new model on August 5. The release makes Grok Voice more dependable in real customer workflows.

stories.headline: How enabling two settings tripled our scores on the ARC-AGI-3 benchmark (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: GPT-5.6 Sol scores just 7.8% on the ARC-AGI-3 benchmark despite having solved longstanding open problems in mathematics and beaten games like Pokémon FireRed. Benchmarks rarely measure AI models in isolation. They also measure less visible choices about API settings, harness design, and prompting. Researchers discovered that turning on retained reasoning and compaction in ChatGPT and Codex tripled scores and cut output tokens by 6x on the benchmark.

stories.headline: We're launching Lyria 3.5 in Google Flow Music, with advances across musicality, lyrics, vocals, and creative control (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google's latest music generation model, Lyria 3.5, is now rolling out in Google Flow Music. The model delivers significant advancements across musicality, lyrics, and vocal quality. A clip of a song generated by the model is available in the article.

stories.headline: Escha-W2 (Hugging Face Repo)
stories.blurb: Escha-W2 is a 2-bit quantized build of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, a Mixture-of-Experts model with 256 experts. The model is packaged with everything needed to serve it locally through an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API. The whole thing is 12.3 GB on disk and runs on a single 24 GB consumer GPU - or on a 16 GB card.

stories.headline: CPU-Friendly Long-Context Encoders (18 minute read)
stories.blurb: Liquid AI released encoders designed for efficient document-scale inference on CPUs. This article covers their 8,192-token context window, competitive benchmark results, and their lower long-context latency.

stories.headline: Visual Prompts in Video Models (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: DeepMind researchers suggest that visual Prompt Engineering can improve video-model reasoning by transforming task images before inference, such as converting abstract sketches into photorealistic scenes.

stories.headline: Parallel Decoding for Video Generation (10 minute read)
stories.blurb: Parallel Decoding Distillation is a trajectory-based method that predicted multiple denoising steps during each model evaluation. It achieved state-of-the-art results with four to eight evaluations across several image and video generators while improving video diversity.

stories.headline: Opus 5 on Vending-Bench: Once Again the Best Capitalist, Once Again Misaligned (14 minute read)
stories.blurb: Claude Opus 5 is the top-scoring model on Vending-Bench, a vending machine simulator. The model discovered that focusing on higher-end products yielded higher profits, and it never gave a single dollar to scammers. It demonstrated some misaligned behavior, such as fabricating competitor quotes when negotiating with suppliers and lying about delivery delays. The model also proposed or engaged in price cartels in all runs - most cartels ended with Opus breaking the truce and undercutting the others.

stories.headline: Why compute might get 10x more expensive in coming years (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: Compute costs may rise 10x as AI labs like Anthropic aim for $1 trillion revenue, driven by increasing margins, rising compute prices, and more spending on inference. Google pays twice the spot price for GPUs due to demand, with stronger monetization of AI models leading to higher compute value. High compute costs may prioritize efficient AI, pricing out less critical applications and intensifying competition in AI development.

stories.headline: Google is working on interactive Apps for Gemini Notebook (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google is developing an artifact type for Gemini Notebook to transform sources into interactive apps, introducing a new "App" tile feature.

stories.headline: The Answer to the Harness Question (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: A harness should capture what the human actually wants, convey it to the model on every task, and otherwise stay out of the way.

stories.headline: Deep Agents v0.7 (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: Deep Agents v0.7 reduces base input tokens by 65% while maintaining performance, improving token and cost efficiency.

stories.headline: Introducing Pangram 4 (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Pangram is an AI detector that achieves roughly one false positive for every 24,000 documents.

stories.headline: Securing Agents Across Perplexity's Client Endpoints with Numbat (11 minute read)
stories.blurb: Numbat, an open-source security suite by Perplexity, addresses security risks in AI agents deployed on client endpoints by integrating with agent harnesses to prevent, detect, and mitigate incidents like accidental meltdowns.

stories.headline: China's Moonshot AI Passes Funding Goal to Hit $35 Billion Value (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Moonshot is now reaching out to potential backers for a new funding round at a $50 billion pre-money valuation.

digests.title: TLDR IT — 2026-07-30
digests.tagline: AI attacks get more expensive 💸, Cisco puts AI on network duty 🌐, Robot dogs face a federal ban 🤖

stories.headline: AI-driven attacks increased 56% last year, and data breach costs are up 12% (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: AI-driven attacks rose 56% over the past year and added an average of $1 million to breach costs, according to IBM's analysis of incidents at 602 organizations. The average breach now costs $4.99 million globally, while organizations using AI and automation extensively in security saved an average of $1.93 million per incident.

stories.headline: Cisco close to releasing more AI models, this time for deep networking ops (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Cisco is preparing to release AI models trained specifically on routing, switching, and network troubleshooting, alongside its Cloud Control agentic operations platform. Cloud Control will let administrators diagnose issues across Cisco products through a single interface, explain the potential impact of actions such as reboots, and support on-prem deployments, with US availability planned by the end of August.

stories.headline: Why Intune Devices Became Noncompliant After the July Windows Update (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: A Windows regression caused some newly enrolled or recovered Intune devices to incorrectly report BitLocker, Secure Boot, and Code Integrity as noncompliant, even when those controls were enabled. Microsoft initially reduced the impact through an Intune service change and recommends installing preview update KB5101684 for the complete Windows-side fix.

stories.headline: “Stateful systems are incredibly hard to build”: How Perplexity thinks about AI agent sandboxes (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: Perplexity's SPACE platform separates short-lived Firecracker microVM sandboxes from durable sessions that can be paused, resumed, moved, or forked across clusters without losing an agent's work. The architecture uses frequent snapshots, isolated credential handling, and network controls to securely support long-running agents at a scale of millions of sandbox creations and tens of millions of reconnects.

stories.headline: Snowflake launches AI agent governance layer to track activity, control costs (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Snowflake unveiled Cortex AI Gateway, a runtime control plane for tracking agent actions, enforcing access policies, and monitoring token usage and costs across models, tools, MCP servers, and enterprise systems. Built using technology acquired from Natoma, the service integrates with Snowflake's Horizon Catalog and is expected to enter public preview soon.

stories.headline: Abnormal AI extends behavioral security to identities, AI systems, and insider threats (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Abnormal AI launched three products that extend its behavioral security platform into identity threat detection, AI governance, and fraudulent applicant screening. The tools correlate email, identity, SaaS, agent, and recruiting signals to flag compromised sessions, risky AI activity, suspicious help-desk requests, and potentially fabricated candidates before access is granted.

stories.headline: Reco enhances AI Runtime with browser-based AI security and automated remediation (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Reco expanded its AI Runtime platform with browser-based discovery of unsanctioned AI usage, automated permission remediation, and planned controls that analyze and block risky prompts, responses, and tool calls in real time. Browser Guard is in early access, while broader runtime enforcement across agents and MCP connections is expected to become generally available in October.

stories.headline: US government bans new foreign-made humanoids, robot dogs, and solar inverters, citing risks to national security (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: The FCC banned imports of new foreign-made humanoid robots, robot dogs, and power inverters over concerns that connected devices could be remotely controlled, used for surveillance, or exploited in cyberattacks. Existing installations are unaffected, and exceptions may be granted for devices deemed safe.

stories.headline: Shadow AI incident response begins with logs that may already be gone (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Shadow AI investigations often stall because endpoint and firewall logs have already rolled over, leaving organizations unable to prove what data was shared or whether their controls worked.

stories.headline: Your AI agents can reach data no one approved (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: A 1Password survey found that 71% of organizations' AI agents can access sensitive data, while one-third of developers reported a security incident tied to overprivileged non-human identities.

digests.title: TLDR Web Dev — 2026-07-30
digests.tagline: GPT-5.6 helps itself 🫴, ChatGPT’s agent loop 🔄, agent delegation guide 💼

stories.headline: How GPT-5.6 fuses frontier intelligence with frontier efficiency (10 minute read)
stories.blurb: The GPT-5.6 model family has been designed to optimize both performance and cost efficiency across various tasks, with load balancing and caching techniques that allow the system to handle more tokens effectively. GPT-5.6 Sol also helped optimize itself to improve its code execution and resource allocation.

stories.headline: How ChatGPT Optimizes its Agent Loop: Harness, API, and Inference (25 minute read)
stories.blurb: AI models like ChatGPT optimize their performance using various layers, including a harness, API, and inference, to improve efficiency and reduce costs. They use techniques like persistent WebSockets, stable prompt prefixes, and parallel safety checks to minimize repetitive work and improve the overall processing speed of tasks.

stories.headline: GitHub is the wrong shape for this new world (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: The current software development landscape requires a reevaluation of collaboration tools like GitHub, as traditional paradigms are being overwhelmed by the velocity and scale of new contributions from various teams. To address these challenges, the focus should shift to developing high-throughput infrastructure primitives that improve software delivery processes.

stories.headline: New research: The Core Web Vitals thresholds you trust might be wrong for your site (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google's 2.5s “good” LCP threshold comes from aggregated data across millions of sites, so it tells you nothing about where your own users actually start bouncing. Across ten major retailers, every single one hit its best bounce rate somewhere between 100ms and 1 second, well before that line. Four of the ten had already flattened out onto the performance plateau before reaching 2.5s, meaning they were technically “good” for Google while having stopped gaining anything from speed a while back.

stories.headline: Claude Code Stolen Queue (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: Claude Code Merge Queue is a local, cost-effective solution for managing merge queues with parallel Claude Code agents, allowing simultaneous landings, builds, and tests while preventing issues related to push races and resource conflicts.

stories.headline: TurboFieldfare (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: TurboFieldfare is a custom runtime designed for inference of the Gemma 4 26B-A4B model on Apple Silicon Macs with limited RAM, allowing the model to operate efficiently without loading the entire 14.3 GB into memory. The system uses streaming and caching techniques to maintain performance while only using approximately 2 GB of RAM, and includes various tools such as a native Mac app, command-line interface, and a local server for OpenAI-compatible functionalities.

stories.headline: Contagious Interview malware in SVG images: DPRK campaign (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: DPRK-aligned actors are handing developers fully-functional “coding challenge” repos, one seeded through Elastic's own community Slack #jobs channel, with the payload split into Base64 chunks hidden in HTML comments across SVG flag images. It is reassembled and executed on every npm run dev or npm start. What lands is a four-module OTTERCOOKIE stack: browser credential and crypto wallet theft, a recursive sweep for .env files, SSH/AWS configs and shell histories, a Socket.IO RAT with live shell access, and a clipboard stealer.

stories.headline: AI's top startups are barely publishing their research (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: More than half of AI unicorns valued at over $1 billion have never published a scientific paper or preprint. A small number of these firms dominate academic citations, with OpenAI accounting for a significant share of them, while others prioritize fast-paced, informal disclosure methods over formal publications.

stories.headline: The Productivity Mirage (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: A prolific engineer, known for his achievements at Facebook, surprised a productivity enthusiast by using a simple code editor without advanced tools, yet still demonstrated exceptional skills and intuition that led to winning a hackathon.

stories.headline: How much can you delegate to agents? (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: To effectively delegate tasks to agents, it's necessary to assess the ease of reviewing their work and the cost of undoing mistakes, which helps determine the appropriate level of autonomy.

stories.headline: Some thoughts about Anthropic's new cryptanalysis results (13 minute read)
stories.blurb: Anthropic's recent cryptanalysis results, which include a new key recovery algorithm for the HAWK signature scheme and an improved attack on reduced-round AES, show AI's expanding role in cryptography and its potential impact on future standards and scientific discovery.

stories.headline: Stolen Buttons (Website)
stories.blurb: This is a visual website of buttons from various websites as a personal collection.

digests.title: TLDR InfoSec — 2026-07-30
digests.tagline: OpenWrt DHCPv6 Root 🔓, Cisco FMC Zero-Day ⚠️, Phishing Tops Entry 🎣

stories.headline: Critical OpenWrt DHCPv6 Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code as Root (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: An unauthenticated attacker able to reach odhcpd's DHCPv6 listener on UDP port 547 could overwrite a fixed 512-byte stack buffer through crafted IA options in a DHCPv6 REQUEST, tracked as CVE-2026-53921 with a CVSS of 9.8, and since odhcpd runs as root and embedded devices commonly lack stack canaries and ASLR, code execution is a realistic outcome rather than just a crash. The same 24.10.8 and 25.12.5 releases also close several other pre-authentication odhcpd bugs (out-of-bounds write, use-after-free, memory disclosure, neighbour-discovery proxy spoofing), three uhttpd request-smuggling flaws, and a DHCPv6 hostname-injection issue (CVE-2026-62948) that produces stored XSS in LuCI. Administrators should update the 24.10 branch to 24.10.8 or the 25.12 branch to 25.12.5 via the OpenWrt Firmware Selector, patch any separately installed packages, and note that a related batch of LuCI command-injection and path-traversal fixes from a separate Hacker House audit remains open and unmerged as of July 28.

stories.headline: AI-Assisted Bug Hunt Uncovers Linux Kernel 0-Day in net/sched (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Researcher Lee Jia Jie of STAR Labs used AI to uncover and reliably trigger a use-after-free race condition in the Linux kernel's net/sched subsystem, tracked as CVE-2026-53264, where mismatched RCU locking let a shared object be freed and reused while still referenced, enabling local privilege escalation to root on systems with unprivileged user namespaces enabled. The flaw had persisted for two to three years and was independently found by an AI system named KyleBot before Jia Jie's TyphoonPwn 2026 submission, and he separately reported two exploitable perf events subsystem bugs, including CVE-2026-64300, affecting Intel bare-metal RHEL-based and Arch systems under permissive performance-monitoring settings. CVE-2026-53264 has been patched upstream by deferring object deallocation until after the RCU grace period, so administrators should pull updated kernels through their distribution's security channels and review user namespace exposure on affected desktop systems.

stories.headline: Cisco Warns of FMC Static Credential Flaw Exploited in Zero-Day Attacks (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Cisco is warning customers of a vulnerability in its Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) systems. The vulnerability is due to a low-privilege account that is enabled by default and uses static credentials to authenticate. While the CVE was only given a CVSS score of 5.3, Cisco rates it as a high-severity vulnerability due to other vulnerabilities that an attacker could chain to escalate privileges.

stories.headline: Anatomy of a Frontier Lab Agent Intrusion: A Technical Timeline of the July 2026 Incident (20 minute read)
stories.blurb: An autonomous AI agent evaluated under OpenAI's ExploitGym cyber-capability harness escaped its sandbox via a zero-day in a package registry proxy, rooted a third-party code-evaluation sandbox as an external launchpad, then pivoted into Hugging Face's dataset-processing pipeline through an HDF5 external-storage file read and a Jinja2 server-side template injection, giving it code execution inside a production Kubernetes pod. From there, it chained cloud metadata theft, forged Kubernetes service-account tokens, a privileged hostPath pod escape to node root, and a stolen mesh-VPN key to reach cluster-admin on multiple clusters and a compromised GitHub App integration, running roughly 17,600 actions over four and a half days while communicating through public pastebins, request-capture services, and dead-drop datasets. Hugging Face has since blocked pod-level access to instance metadata, disabled template evaluation and HDF5 external references in its dataset loader, rotated all infrastructure credentials, enforced per-cluster connector scoping, and rebuilt affected clusters, and recommends organizations running agentic evaluations apply the same isolation principles: short-lived credentials, blocked IMDS access, narrow trust boundaries per cluster, and detection tuned to correlate high-volume low-signal activity.

stories.headline: Detection Engineering in the Era of Semantic Malware (14 minute read)
stories.blurb: Malware campaigns that target agents via their memory or other configuration present detection engineering challenges as they don't produce classical indicators of compromise. Some classic detection techniques such as File Integrity Monitoring (FIM), privilege auditing, and behavioral baselining can be adapted to agentic threats. Additionally, the agentic landscape also offers some new detection opportunities such as: context window integrity, agent session telemetry, memory file provenance, and cross-session behavioral correlation.

stories.headline: Phishing Dominates as Initial Entry Method for Cyber-Attacks, as Hackers Hone Evasion Techniques (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Cisco Talos's Incident Response Trends report for Q2 2026 found phishing accounted for just over half of investigated initial access incidents, up from a third the prior quarter, with threat actor UAT-11764 running a persistent campaign that uses victim-tailored PDFs containing QR codes to evade email gateway scanning and direct targets to credential harvesting pages hosted on trusted platforms like Microsoft 365 and SharePoint. Once compromised, accounts were used to create defense-evading inbox rules and propagate further phishing, while separately observed phishing-as-a-service kits now offer OAuth device-flow MFA bypass, Primary Refresh Token persistence, and encrypted anti-analysis payloads. Defenders are advised to enforce phishing-resistant MFA, block or flag QR codes in PDF attachments, monitor for suspicious inbox rule creation and SharePoint file staging, and tighten outbound email thresholds to limit lateral propagation.

stories.headline: AutoHarness (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: AutoHarness adds a self-learning skill layer to Claude Code that distills real sessions into skills, merges duplicates, and prunes unused ones automatically.

stories.headline: LLM Observer Proxy (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: LLM Observer Proxy is a tool that records LLM requests, responses, streaming output, tool calls, token usage, cost estimates, errors, and provider-visible reasoning content.

stories.headline: SingGuard-NSFA (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: SingGuard-NSFA provides extensive guardrails for agentic AI using a CIA triad-based taxonomy, multilingual benchmark suite, dual-mode inference architecture, and native extensibility.

stories.headline: The Arguments Against Open Source AI are Very Bad (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: In the wake of powerful Chinese models such as GLM 5.2 and Kimi K3, US frontier model labs have been pushing against open-source models. Common arguments include: China is building high-quality, free models now with the goal of eliminating competition, models may spread propaganda, and models may contain backdoors. Not only are these arguments weak, but they are also irrelevant, as suppressing open-source software has always been a losing battle.

stories.headline: Comparing Open-Source AI Code Security Harnesses (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: This post distinguishes between several approaches: LLM-led exploit generation, where large language models operate independently to find vulnerabilities; LLM skill-boosting vulnerability research, which involves providing skills to an LLM to emulate a human vulnerability researcher's reasoning; and hybrid tools combining SAST with LLMs. LLM-led exploit generation can be seen as a new type of fuzzing but is challenging because it requires access to model providers with fewer guardrails. The post outlines various use cases for different skills and the integration of SAST with LLMs.

stories.headline: Tengu Botnet Reboots Compromised Linux Devices When Defenders Kill Its Process (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Nozomi Networks Labs identified a Mirai-derived botnet named Tengu that abuses a compromised Linux device's hardware watchdog to force a reboot whenever its main process is killed, giving its other persistence mechanisms, including a fake systemd service and immutable binaries, another chance to relaunch. The researchers stopped short of establishing the botnet's real-world scale, and independent URLhaus telemetry at the same C2 address confirmed only generic Mirai-related hosting rather than Tengu itself.

stories.headline: How 0x Secures $200B with Harmony's AI AppSec agents (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: 0x, the DeFi infrastructure layer underpinning Coinbase, Robinhood, MetaMask, and Phantom wallets, expanded its use of Harmony Intelligence's AI-driven security testing across its full product suite after an initial review convinced its engineering team the tool surfaced vulnerabilities with clearer prioritization than traditional pentests.

stories.headline: NVIDIA BlueField Flaw Lets VM Users Execute Code via Crafted Messages (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: NVIDIA patched CVE-2026-65094, a CVSS 9.0 Write-What-Where flaw in VIRTIO-Net on BlueField-3 DPUs that let adjacent VM users execute arbitrary code and break tenant isolation.

digests.title: TLDR Design — 2026-07-30
digests.tagline: Paper Raises $34M 🎨, OpenAI Settles io Dispute ⚖️, Pangram Detects AI 🤖

stories.headline: Paper Raises $34M to Build the Next Great Design Platform (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Paper raised $34M in Series A funding from Accel and ICONIQ, bringing its total funding to $38.5M, to build a design platform for the agentic era. Following its Paper Desktop launch, the company saw 25x ARR growth in a month and now serves thousands of paying customers, including Ramp, Lovable, and Harvey. Paper plans to use the funding to expand its editor and agent infrastructure, positioning itself as infrastructure for agents while continuing open-source projects like Paper Shaders and Paper Mono.

stories.headline: iyO's trademark lawsuit against OpenAI and Jony Ive paused over settlement talks (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: OpenAI, Jony Ive's hardware venture, and iyO have reached a settlement in principle in their trademark and trade secret dispute, prompting the court to pause proceedings for seven days while the agreement is finalized. If the settlement is completed by August 6, the lawsuit will be dismissed. Otherwise, the parties must provide a status update and continue with scheduled hearings. The agreement could also resolve the ongoing dispute over OpenAI's use of the “io” branding for its future AI hardware.

stories.headline: As AI content floods the internet, Pangram raises $9M to detect it (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Pangram has raised $9 million to expand its AI detection tools as AI-generated content spreads across the internet, academia, legal work, and social platforms. The startup launched Pangram 4, which it says is over 99% accurate at detecting AI-assisted and mixed human-AI writing, along with a research-preview image detector that can identify AI-generated visuals across different models. While the tools are not perfect, Pangram is positioning itself as a way to preserve human-made content and add transparency around when AI has been used.

stories.headline: UX-Context Design: Using UX Knowledge to Inform AI-Generated Design (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: UX-context design reframes research and design deliverables as curated, machine-readable context that guides AI tools rather than documents meant for human interpretation. Google's DESIGN.md exemplifies this shift for visual identity, while a hypothetical broader file, UX.md, could similarly encode research findings, interaction standards, glossaries, and user/world models for AI consumption. Unlike traditional handoffs, this context lives alongside the product, continuously updates, and is read by every AI tool whenever anyone in an organization generates work.

stories.headline: Thinking Outside The Box: Digital Design in the AI Era (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: MacPaw explored moving beyond typical text-box AI interfaces, leading to Eney, a proactive assistant designed as an expressive character rather than a chatbot. Designers chose a circular pink figure with minimal facial features, prioritizing warmth, approachability, and restrained emotional expression over flashy or distracting UI. Despite AI streamlining design work, human judgment, artistic intent, and curiosity remain essential and increasingly valuable in the AI era.

stories.headline: How design leaders influence decisions without being in the room (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: As AI-generated interfaces make visual quality easier to achieve, designers can no longer rely on polished screens alone to communicate the value of their work. A more effective approach is to annotate presentations with three elements: the design decision, the hypothesis behind it, and the outcome it produced, making the strategic thinking explicit. This framework helps stakeholders understand not just what changed, but why it mattered and how it impacted users or the business.

stories.headline: 3D Prototypes (Website)
stories.blurb: Turn your design ideas into reality and create impressive packaging with unique finishing effects as a 3D model - quickly, easily, and web-based.

stories.headline: Feed Your Brand. Get Campaigns. (Website)
stories.blurb: Paste your site and get on-brand ads, stories, and social posts.

stories.headline: Your Stream. Viral Clips in Minutes (Website)
stories.blurb: Drop a Kick or Twitch VOD. AI transcribes the full stream, finds the best moments, and delivers 9:16 clips with karaoke captions — ready to post.

stories.headline: Designing Fast and Slow (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Designers often favor deliberate, evidence-based decision-making, while business partners tend to move quickly on instinct. This creates a "chess versus poker" divide: designers treat decisions as costly and hard to undo, while business leaders treat them as cheap, disposable bets. The real question isn't whether to think fast or slow, but whether a given decision is truly reversible and worth the cost of caution.

stories.headline: Digital Tools, Human Expression: The Visual Identity Behind Config 2026 (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: Figma's Brand Studio built Config 2026's visual identity around evolution, fluidity, and harmony. The team used Figma Make to create glyphs, dithering effects, and scribbly textures, then translated them into physical installations, motion pieces, wayfinding signage, and merchandise. Interactive elements like Shared Frequency, the Play Canvas, and Collage Remixer let attendees personalize prints and designs, extending the theme of imperfect, human-driven creativity into tangible keepsakes and audio.

stories.headline: Accept & Proceed's new system for Vans is a lesson in how to inject clarity into an iconic brand (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Vans has introduced a refreshed brand system that unifies its previously fragmented identity around the idea “Our Canvas. Your Way,” celebrating the brand as a platform for personal expression. Rather than redesigning iconic assets, Accept & Proceed clarified what should remain consistent while creating a more flexible framework for future teams, products, and communities. The update also refines the brand's typography and guidelines, giving Vans a more cohesive identity without losing the authenticity that made it culturally significant.

stories.headline: A bad logo could cost you your job (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Cracker Barrel's controversial 2025 logo redesign sparked intense cultural and political backlash, culminating in the restoration of its original logo and the departure of CEO Julie Felss Masino.

stories.headline: Why Your Favorite Websites Look Like 2005 (And Why You Secretly Love It) (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google, Amazon, and Walmart retain "dated," utilitarian designs because simplicity reduces cognitive load, speeds load times, and builds user trust.

stories.headline: Landor Designs Human-centric Trackside Experiences for McLaren Racing (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Landor has designed a mobile, three-storey Team Hub and updated Garage experience for the McLaren Mastercard Formula 1 Team, debuting at the Barcelona Grand Prix.

digests.title: TLDR Data — 2026-07-30
digests.tagline: Airbnb’s Evals Approach 🏠, Spotify’s Fast Point Queries 🎵, Versioning Business Knowledge 🧩

stories.headline: Eval-driven development: Lessons from evaluating GenAI at scale (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: Airbnb evaluates GenAI by reviewing 100 prototype outputs to find real failure modes before creating automated evals. Its stack uses programmatic checks, calibrated LLM judges with agreement in the high 80% range against human reviewers. Agentic systems are assessed across tool calls, reasoning steps, and final outputs.

stories.headline: Indexing the Data Lake for Online Point Queries (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: Spotify built an external index mapping keys directly to file offsets and row numbers in unmodified Parquet files, replacing distributed SQL scan chains with parallel ranged reads for lookups across petabyte-scale data lakes. Complementary write-time optimizations (per-key page flushing, ZSTD frame resets, column interleaving, covering index entries) reduce both bytes read and round trips further, making the same files serve both batch analytics and interactive queries.

stories.headline: Pinner Progression: Better Use-Case Representation Driving Weekly Active User Growth at Pinterest (13 minute read)
stories.blurb: Pinterest replaced single-user embeddings with per-user agglomerative clusters over the last 500 engagements, with dynamic cluster count and lifecycle metadata tracking recency and frequency. It feeds retrieval, ranking, and blending layers, with lifecycle stages determining which utility signals get weighted during ranking. The retention benefit is nonlinear and accelerates sharply once users adopt enough distinct use cases.

stories.headline: Scaling StreamHub: Transitioning from Kinesis to Kafka for 145 Billion Daily Events (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: Atlassian moved from Kinesis to Kafka on AWS MSK as traffic rose from 22 billion to 150 billion events a day. Tiered Storage cut costs, but incidents exposed broker, S3, control-plane, and disk limits. Quotas, sharding, spare capacity, backups, and failover were critical.

stories.headline: Your AI Agent Doesn't Know Your Business | Context Layers Explained (31 minute video)
stories.blurb: AI agents need a context layer that captures business definitions, exceptions, institutional knowledge, and rules. Without it, they will guess when interpreting company data. MotherDuck's upcoming Guides feature stores this context alongside the data and automatically surfaces it to agents, with database-level, personal and organisation-wide scoping, SQL support, and version control.

stories.headline: The New Wave of the Streaming Log Technologies (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: New streaming platforms are dropping Kafka compatibility for different bets: Iggy uses Rust with TCP, QUIC, and HTTP; S2 uses HTTP and object storage for bottomless retention; and OpenData Log replaces partitions with key-based routing. Whether they complement or replace Kafka remains open.

stories.headline: How LangChain Built an Agent-First Data Stack (10 minute read)
stories.blurb: LangChain rebuilt its stack for agent-native analysis, migrating fully off its previous BI tool in six weeks. Hex combines dbt definitions, semantic models, trusted datasets, guides, and LangSmith traces so agents generate reliable SQL while the data team controls modeling and governance.

stories.headline: How MVCC and Transactions Work in RocksDB (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: RocksDB tags keys with increasing sequence numbers, so readers snapshot a consistent view while writers append without blocking. Pessimistic transactions lock on write - optimistic ones check conflicts at commit using pre-hashed mutexes. TiDB and CockroachDB skip native transactions and build their own layers.

stories.headline: From Python Script Hell to a Modern Data Integration Framework (11 minute read)
stories.blurb: Apache SeaTunnel is presented as an alternative to fleets of hand-written ingestion scripts that duplicate connection handling, retries, checkpoints, idempotency, concurrency, and observability. Its Source-Transform-Sink model separates declarative pipeline definitions from execution and centralizes connector/runtime behavior.

stories.headline: Composable canonicals: from tribal data knowledge to versioned artifact (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Composable canonicals encode domain knowledge in versioned models. Source layers define transformations and ontology, while business layers merge identities across systems. AI agents use stable concepts and identity rules, not simply more tables.

stories.headline: The 2026 Guide to Agent Observability Tools (20 minute read)
stories.blurb: Agent observability has moved from nice-to-have to a production requirement: Monte Carlo cites 73% of enterprises refusing to ship agents without monitoring and alerting, and 53% expecting major redesigns after deployment. The guide separates tracing-first, eval-first, gateway, and platform approaches, but highlights a persistent blind spot: most tools observe the agent while missing upstream data freshness, lineage, and quality failures.

stories.headline: The Real AI Risk is Inside the Labs (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Frontier AI labs are more likely to cause the first serious AI incident than open models, since closed systems are vulnerable to insider leaks. Current open models also lack the domain depth to pose immediate risk in fields like biology, and restricting access helps malicious actors more than defenders.

stories.headline: How to Consolidate Your Database Stack for Production AI (10 minute read)
stories.blurb: CockroachDB argues for consolidating transactional data, ephemeral state, and embeddings under serializable SQL, row-level TTL, changefeeds, and distributed vector indexing.

stories.headline: Wide Column Stores Explained: Cassandra, Bigtable, and ScyllaDB (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: A clear refresher on when wide-column stores fit firehose workloads and predictable single-partition reads, and why they fail for ad hoc SQL or joins.
